To see how we can draw on the logic of both the closed and small open
economies and apply these insights to the United States, consider how a monetary contraction affects the economy in the short run. In a closed economy, a
monetary contraction raises the interest rate, lowers investment, and thus lowers aggregate income. In a small open economy with a floating exchange rate,
a monetary contraction raises the exchange rate, lowers net exports, and thus
lowers aggregate income. The interest rate is unaffected, however, because it is
determined by world financial markets.
